correction: The historical 27-Feb departure is NOT inherited. Previous v001 tested hull survival but failed to close the Branch-specific movement and strategic-release chain for Tone and Chikuma.

branch_conflict.Tone_Chikuma_03Feb: Both were committed as heavy-cruiser scouts/screen in the Branch first-line carrier battle on 3 Feb, unlike their historical February movements.
branch_conflict.postbattle: The Branch carrier force then withdrew west after severe air-group attrition; HAILSTONE closeout only states that major surface units were west of Truk and dispersing toward Palau/Philippines/home-area support nodes. It does not place Tone or Chikuma at Lingga on a dated chain.
branch_conflict.standing_gate: Indian Ocean second surface reinforcement remained HOLD under Central-Pacific priority through the last pre-HAILSTONE synchronized state. A commerce-raider detachment using two first-line carrier-scout cruisers requires an explicit new release decision.
branch_conflict.historical_schedule_not_portable: Historically Tone left Truk on 1 Feb and reached Lingga on 21 Feb, while Chikuma completed a Kure refit and reached Lingga on 13 Feb. Those histories are impossible to copy after the Branch 3-Feb carrier engagement.

centered_strategic_judgment: After the Branch 3-Feb carrier battle, subsequent Marshall/CATCHPOLE loss and HAILSTONE neutralization of Truk, Combined Fleet has a stronger reason than history to retain Tone/Chikuma for mobile-fleet scouting, screening and reconstitution. Therefore the historical three-heavy-cruiser commerce raid is centered on HOLD/NO-GO at 27 Feb unless a later explicit release gate reverses that judgment.
